newsitem.title: CANADA: Placer raises Cerro Crucitas gold estimate.
newsitem.headline: Placer raises Cerro Crucitas gold estimate.

text.p: Gold giant Placer Dome Inc said Wednesday it had increased the resource estimate for its Cerro Crucitas property in Costa Rica to 2.2 million ounces of gold from 1.8 million ounces.

In addition, the company said construction of facilities at its Nevada project was three months ahead of schedule and slated for start-up in April. The project is expected to be US$50 million under budget.
The project is held by the Cortez joint venture, in which Placer has 60 percent and RTZ Corp Plc -CRA Ltd 40 percent.
The project combines the Pipeline and South Pipeline gold deposits. Placer raised the mining rate during the first five years to 675,000 ounces a year, up from 575,000 ounces.
Placer said drilling continues at its Donlin Creek exploration property in Alaska where it estimates a resource of 3.6 million ounces of gold.

In addition, Placer is continuing negotiations with the majority shareholder of the Marcopper mine in the Philippines with a view to divesting its 40 percent stake after a major spill of mine waste there earlier this year.
